clue.text: Decline to fall in love? Just the opposite

indicators.note: in would put the first word inside the second, but the following phrase turns that round
this phrase reverses the stated arrangement, so the fall-word goes around the love-word instead

parts.note: to fall is to drop
love is nil in tennis scoring, the letter O

explanation.surface: A suitor turns down the chance to fall in love, preferring the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, 'fall in love' puts DROP inside O; 'Just the opposite' says put O inside DROP instead.
explanation.definitionFit: To droop is to sag or sink, a synonym of decline.

clue.text: Could be said soft fruit seems to vanish

indicators.note: could be says the letters of said may be rearranged

parts.note: p is piano, soft in music
a pear is a fruit

explanation.surface: Ripe fruit, it is said, seems to disappear quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Could be' rearranges SAID to give DISA; 'seems' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To disappear is to vanish, a synonym.

clue.text: In an animal book a picture of him?

definitions.text: In an animal book a picture of him?

indicators.note: In tells us the answer sits inside the words book a picture

explanation.surface: A natural history book would show this creature.
explanation.definitionFit: An African forest mammal related to the giraffe, as shown in an animal book.

clue.text: Underground transporters converted into pipes

indicators.note: converted means the letters of into pipes are changed into a new form

explanation.surface: Mining equipment turned into piping.
explanation.walkthrough: PIT PONIES were ponies used in coal mines to haul loads underground.
explanation.definitionFit: Small horses that hauled coal in British mines carried loads below ground.

clue.text: Copy about yield

parts.note: re means concerning or about
produce is what land yields, its crop

explanation.surface: A note on copying a report about crop yields.
explanation.definitionFit: To reproduce something is to make a copy of it, a synonym.

clue.text: Sign measures as stiff as these

parts.note: the Ram is Aries, a zodiac sign
a rod is an old measure of length

explanation.surface: A signpost giving distances, as rigid as the posts themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: A ROD is an old British measure of length, about five metres.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'as stiff as a ramrod' uses the gun-loading rod as the image of stiffness.

clue.text: Sharp officer in a boat

indicators.note: in places the officer inside the boat

parts.note: a punt is a flat-bottomed boat
Gen is short for General

explanation.surface: A keen general sitting in a small boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Pungent means sharp in smell or taste, or biting.

clue.text: Root for the Roman Poet, as cockneys might say

indicators.note: cockney speech drops the opening H, so the name is said that way

parts.note: Horace was the great Roman lyric poet

explanation.surface: A fan cheers on the Roman poet in a London accent.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys (east Londoners) drop their H's, so HORACE comes out as 'ORACE.
explanation.definitionFit: Orris is the fragrant root of a kind of iris used in perfumery.

clue.text: Rebuked for such a plaits-on-top hair-style?

definitions.meaning: hair braided and pinned on top of the head

explanation.surface: Told off for wearing braids piled high.
explanation.definitionFit: To upbraid is to scold; read as UP BRAIDED it is plaited hair worn high.

clue.text: She gets one in, besides

indicators.note: in puts one inside the besides-word

parts.note: else means otherwise or besides
one is I in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A woman takes someone in, as well.
explanation.definitionFit: Elsie is a woman's name, so she is a fair definition.

clue.text: Singer in a humble dwelling?

parts.note: a sailors' work-song singer whose title can be read as a man living in a hut

explanation.surface: A vocalist living modestly in a cottage.
explanation.walkthrough: A shanty is both a sea song and a crude hut, so the singer of sea songs reads as a man in a hut.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailor who led the crew's work songs at sea had this title, punningly also a hut-dweller.

clue.text: Corps transport provides a puzzle

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
a bus is a means of public transport

explanation.surface: An army unit's vehicles turn out to be baffling.
explanation.walkthrough: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture-and-letter riddle is a kind of puzzle.

clue.text: First airman going round the edge

indicators.note: the officer surrounds the edge-word, enclosing it

parts.note: PO is a Pilot Officer, an RAF rank
a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: A leading pilot flies around the boundary of the airfield.
explanation.walkthrough: PO is the abbreviation for Pilot Officer, a junior Royal Air Force rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian for first, used in English for the leading part in a duet or the top player.

clue.text: Exaggerate like a monarch

definitions.meaning: to make more of something than it deserves
a ruler stands above the nation, over the state

explanation.surface: To boast as grandly as a king might.
explanation.definitionFit: To overstate is to overemphasise or exaggerate; a monarch, by a cryptic split, is placed over a state.

clue.text: Subjects of Wilde's careful choice

parts.note: Oscar Wilde said a man cannot be too careful in choosing his foes

explanation.surface: The people Oscar Wilde picked with great care.
explanation.walkthrough: From Wilde's The Picture of Dorian Gray: 'A man cannot be too careful in the choice of his enemies.'
explanation.definitionFit: Wilde's quip names foes as the people one should select most carefully.

clue.text: Source of report of increase in population?

definitions.meaning: a report is a loud bang, whose source is a blast
a sudden boom in numbers, as in the phrase population boom

explanation.surface: The origin of a document about rising population figures.
explanation.definitionFit: A blast makes a report or bang; a sudden population rise is called a population explosion.

clue.text: Rants about terrible disasters — ship missing

indicators.note: terrible signals the letters of disasters are mixed up

parts.note: SS is steamship

explanation.surface: Angry outbursts about dreadful catastrophes at sea when a vessel vanishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' tells you to remove SS (steamship) from DISASTERS; 'terrible' says rearrange what is left (DIATER S) into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tirade is a long angry speech, a rant.

clue.text: Parliamentarian's clue for "R"

definitions.meaning: a supporter of Parliament in the English Civil War; the 's is is
the letter R is the head, or first letter, of round

explanation.surface: An MP gives a hint for a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: Roundheads were Parliament's supporters in the English Civil War (1640s), named for their cropped hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Cromwell's side were nicknamed for close-cropped heads; a clue for R could be the first letter of round.

clue.text: Apes tread uncertainly when kept apart

indicators.note: uncertainly suggests the letters of Apes tread move about unsteadily

explanation.surface: Monkeys walk unsteadily when held in separate cages.
explanation.definitionFit: Separated means divided or kept apart.

clue.text: Counter-attack ready to fall on East German borders

indicators.note: the ready-word borders, or encloses, the German word

parts.note: fruit that is ripe is ready to fall
Ost is German for east

explanation.surface: An offensive is poised to strike at the frontiers of East Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East German' is not the old country but the German word for east, OST.
explanation.definitionFit: A riposte in fencing is a quick return thrust, a counter-attack.

clue.text: Exonerates river police (military) on the way up

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, England
MP is military police

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read upward, backwards

parts.note: St is street, a way

explanation.surface: Military police by a river clear people of blame as they climb.
explanation.walkthrough: The EXE is a river in Devon. 'on the way up' gives TS, ST (street) reversed in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To exempt is to free from an obligation, close to exonerate.

clue.text: Finished? This time-keeper's ready to go

definitions.meaning: a clock or watch that has had its spring tightened is ready to run

explanation.surface: Done? This clock is set to start.
explanation.definitionFit: Something concluded has been brought to an end; a wound clock has its spring tightened.

clue.text: He gets award, perhaps for what causes 14

indicators.note: perhaps hints the letters of He award could be differently arranged

explanation.surface: A man gets a prize for causing a blast.
explanation.walkthrough: 14 is the answer to 14 Down, a blast.
explanation.definitionFit: A warhead is the explosive tip of a missile that produces the blast.

clue.text: He makes inordinate gains for Peter (and one's twisting)

indicators.note: twisting tells us to scramble the letters of the words before it

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Peter is accused of excessive gains while one person is distorting matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisting' rearranges FOR, PETER and I (one).
explanation.definitionFit: A profiteer is someone who makes excessive profits, especially in scarcity.

clue.text: Play on words one has about Carthaginian

parts.note: a pun is a play on words
one is I in Roman numerals
c, circa, means about

explanation.surface: Someone's wordplay concerning the ancient city of Carthage.
explanation.walkthrough: The Punic Wars were fought between Rome and Carthage.
explanation.definitionFit: Punic is the adjective for ancient Carthage and its people.

clue.text: Peaceful girl

definitions.meaning: the name comes from Greek eirene, peace, also the root of irenic

explanation.definitionFit: Irene is a girl's name from the Greek goddess of peace, hence peaceful.

clue.text: Delightful start — end is gloomy

indicators.note: start means take the first letter of Delightful

parts.note: the rear is the end of something

explanation.surface: A lovely opening but the ending is dismal.
explanation.definitionFit: Drear is a poetic word for dreary, bleak and gloomy.

clue.text: Poet's lament, say, in a cathedral city

indicators.note: in puts the example word inside the city

parts.note: Ely in Cambridgeshire is a cathedral city
eg means for example, say

explanation.surface: A poet's mournful verse set in a cathedral town.
explanation.walkthrough: ELY is a small cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: An elegy is a mournful poem, a lament.

clue.text: "A happy — to hear" (Housman)

parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank from a line in A. E. Housman's poem about Bredon Hill

explanation.surface: A quotation from Housman with a word left out.
explanation.walkthrough: The line is from Bredon Hill in A Shropshire Lad: church bells make 'a happy noise to hear'.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word in Housman's line about the bells is a sound or din.

clue.text: As does the Old Testament judicial model

definitions.meaning: the Old Testament comes before the New
an earlier court ruling that later cases follow

explanation.surface: The Old Testament as a pattern for later law.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as PRECEDE NT: the Old Testament comes before the New Testament (NT).
explanation.definitionFit: A legal precedent is a prior ruling serving as a model; the Old Testament goes before the New.

clue.text: Concentrated study by Poles indeed

parts.note: to con is to study or learn

indicators.note: in signals the poles going inside the deed-word

parts.note: taken as written
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Someone studies Polish people thoroughly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'indeed' splits as 'in deed': N and S (the poles) go in DEED.
explanation.definitionFit: Condensed means reduced in volume, made concentrated.

clue.text: Dull publicity for a nymph

parts.note: dry means dull and uninteresting
an ad, short for advertisement, gives publicity

explanation.surface: A tedious advertising campaign for a woodland spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: A dryad is a wood nymph in Greek myth.
